race.name: Nanaimo Unpaved
race.tagline: A real Vancouver Island race through 2025, now absent from the official BC Gravel Series calendar.

vitals.course_status_reason: The official BC Gravel Series lists four 2026 events and Nanaimo Unpaved is not one of them. Its archived page remains dated June 15, 2025.
vitals.field_size: 107 timed finishers in the 2024 results; 2025 field not stated on the organizer page
vitals.aid_stations: Supported series format; archived page does not list station locations
vitals.cutoff_time: 2025 awards at 3:00 PM; no course-specific cutoff published

climate.description: The last edition ran in mid-June. Coastal rain, cool starts, and changing forest-road traction mattered more than altitude; no future date exists to support a current forecast.
challenges: Limited cell coverage in forest terrain

terrain.surface: The 2025 race used Vancouver Island gravel and dirt roads from the Nanaimo MX Association venue. The organizer published three route distances but no elevation totals on the archived page.

gravel_god_rating.score_note: The verified event had three substantial routes, timed results, a race bible, and BC Gravel Series support in distinctive island terrain. No current edition, no organizer-published gain, and a regional field hold it at 57 and Tier 3.

biased_opinion.summary: Nanaimo Unpaved was not fabricated: the organizer's archived page, race bible, and timed results prove the event. The current database mistake is different—it treats a 2025 race as if it still has a future edition. The BC Gravel Series replaced the calendar slot with a new Port Alberni event but does not call it a rename, so these identities stay separate.
weaknesses: No official elevation totals on the archived page
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Preserve the race history, but do not sell a current Nanaimo plan or silently rename it West Coast Slugger.

final_verdict.one_liner: A legitimate island race that belongs in the archive until the organizer brings it back.
final_verdict.should_you_race: There is no current edition. For the active series, look at West Coast Slugger, Burnt Bridge, River City, or Forbidden Gravel.
final_verdict.alternatives: For the new 2026 Port Alberni event, compare West Coast Slugger.

logistics.airport: Nanaimo Airport or ferry access from the mainland; no current race travel should be booked
logistics.lodging_strategy: The archived venue was at the Nanaimo MX Association; wait for an official return before reserving
logistics.food: The 2025 itinerary listed food and drinks from 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM
logistics.packet_pickup: 2025 pickup ran Saturday in Nanaimo and Sunday at the venue
logistics.parking: Archived race-bible details only; no current operation

eligibility.status_note: The archived event page remains dated June 15, 2025. The official 2026 series schedule omits Nanaimo and introduces West Coast Slugger in Port Alberni as a new event.

history.founder: Panache Cycling Sports and BC Gravel Series
history.origin_story: Nanaimo Unpaved joined the Vancouver Island gravel series with timed editions in 2024 and 2025.
notable_moments: The 2025 edition offered 42.12 km, 85 km, and 110.8 km routes
history.reputation: A short-lived but legitimate Vancouver Island series stop.

course_description.character: A three-distance coastal-forest gravel event from the Nanaimo MX venue, with the archived long route covering 110.8 km.

suffering_zones.label: MX Venue Start
suffering_zones.desc: All 2025 riders self-seeded for a mass start from the Nanaimo motocross venue.

suffering_zones.label: Forest-Road Middle
suffering_zones.desc: Remote Vancouver Island gravel and changing coastal traction created the race's central load.

suffering_zones.label: Esperto Return
suffering_zones.desc: The long route returned toward the venue after more than 100 km of mixed forest road.

course_description.signature_challenge: Managing coastal traction and self-sufficiency across a long island forest route.

guide_variables.race_distance: 68.8 miles (110.8 km) at the last edition
guide_variables.race_terrain: Vancouver Island forest gravel and dirt roads
guide_variables.race_weather: Coastal rain and cool-start risk when last held

non_negotiables.why: Nanaimo is absent from the official 2026 schedule.

non_negotiables.requirement: Separate identity from West Coast Slugger
non_negotiables.why: The organizer calls the Port Alberni event new and never states that it is a Nanaimo rename.

migration_notes: Replaced the unsupported generic 50-mile/3,500-foot profile with official 2025 route distances
Marked the race inactive because it is absent from the official 2026 series schedule
Kept West Coast Slugger separate because the organizer calls it a new event rather than a rename

logistics.explanation: Nanaimo has airport and ferry access, but Vancouver Island travel still takes more planning than a mainland local race.

length.explanation: The archived 110.8 km Esperto route is 68.8 miles, inside the rubric's 60-100-mile band.

technicality.explanation: The 110.8 km Esperto used forest and logging roads with coastal traction, without organizer claims of extreme singletrack.

elevation.explanation: The organizer does not publish total gain on the archived page; a conservative 2 replaces the unsupported 3,500-foot claim.

climate.explanation: Vancouver Island rain, cool starts, and changing forest traction are meaningful preparation constraints.

altitude.explanation: The coastal Nanaimo setting does not create an altitude-training requirement.

adventure.explanation: Remote Vancouver Island forest roads and coastal scenery give the event real destination character.

prestige.explanation: BC Gravel Series affiliation is credible regionally, but two editions do not create national prestige.

race_quality.explanation: The 2025 operation included a race bible, timed results, 3 routes, packet pickup, food, and awards.

experience.explanation: The Vancouver Island setting and 3-distance event provide a memorable regional day beyond a barebones gravel start.

community.explanation: The 2024 results list 107 riders and the BC Gravel Series has a local base, but the event's run was short.

field_depth.explanation: The 2024 results show 107 riders, but not an elite or nationally deep field.

value.explanation: The BC Gravel Series offered 3 routes, support, and food, but the archived page does not expose a verifiable final price.

expenses.explanation: Ferry or flight costs to Vancouver Island make the total trip moderate even for nearby riders.

topics.equipment: Tires and layers for coastal conditions
